# Counters

Every counter Cavalry has, from `counters.toml`, the single source ([ADR 0012](../decisions/0012-lay-out-the-counters-file.md)). The driver publishes each one in the [counters file](counters-file.md). A static counter is allocated when the file is created, in the record whose index is its id, and its label is its name. An instance counter is allocated per key when its instance is created, and its label is the name, a space, and the key's text as the doc column defines it. A `counter` never decreases while allocated; a `gauge` moves both ways. This page is generated by `scripts/gen-counters.py`: edit `counters.toml`, never this page, and `just lint-counters` fails when the two differ.

| Id | Name | Kind | Scope | What a change means | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | `counters.allocated` | gauge | static | Metadata records in the allocated state, this counter's own record included. |  |
| 1 | `counters.allocation_failed` | counter | static | Counter allocations refused because every record was in use: the counters file is full, and whatever needed the counter was refused with it. | The counters file is full and new publications and subscriptions are refused until a counter is freed: close what is not used; the capacity is fixed in this version. |
| 2 | `publication.position` | gauge | instance | The producer position of one publication's log buffer, written by the driver on its duty cycle from a load it makes at most once per millisecond, so at most a millisecond behind the publisher (ADR 0022); key: correlation id (i64), session id (i32), stream id (i32), little-endian; label text: the three in decimal, space-separated. |  |
| 3 | `publication.limit` | gauge | instance | The position up to which one publication may write: the slowest subscriber's position plus the publication window, written by the driver; key and label as publication.position. | If publication.position sits at publication.limit, a subscriber is slow or stopped: compare the subscription.position counters of the stream and look at that subscriber. |
| 4 | `subscription.position` | gauge | instance | How far one subscription has read one publication's stream, written by the subscriber after each poll with a release store; key: correlation id (i64), session id (i32), stream id (i32), little-endian; label text: the three in decimal, space-separated. | A subscription.position that does not move while publication.position does is a subscriber that stopped polling; its publisher will be back-pressured when it reaches the window. |
| 5 | `publication.unblocked` | counter | static | Stale claims the driver turned into padding frames because a publisher claimed and did not commit within the unblock timeout (spec/log-buffer.md, The driver). | A publisher process died or stalled between claim and commit; find it from the publication whose position stopped moving, and keep claim and commit on one thread with nothing blocking between them. |
| 6 | `log_buffer.rejected_position` | counter | static | Subscriber positions the driver found outside the spec's bounds and refused to use; the client that wrote one is evicted (ADR 0010). | A client wrote an impossible position: a buggy binding or a hostile process. The driver's log names the client; rebuild or remove it. |
| 7 | `log_buffer.rejected_tail` | counter | static | Tail counters the driver found inconsistent with the active term count and refused to use; the publication is closed (ADR 0010). | A publisher wrote an impossible tail: a buggy binding or a hostile process. The driver's log names the publication; rebuild or remove the client. |
| 8 | `log_buffer.rejected_frame` | counter | static | Frames a subscriber found outside spec/frame.md's bounds in a term and reported; nothing after such a frame is delivered on that image. | A publisher wrote a corrupt frame, or a term was overwritten: check publication.unblocked and the driver's log for the publication. |
| 9 | `command_ring.unblocked` | counter | static | Padding records the driver wrote over a claim in the command ring that a client made and did not commit within the unblock timeout (spec/command-ring.md, Unblocking). | A client process died or stalled between claiming and committing a command; its own driver timeout closes it. If this repeats, find the client that keeps restarting and look at what stops it between claim and commit. |
| 10 | `command_ring.rejected_tail` | counter | static | Tail positions the driver found outside the command ring's bounds when it unblocked and refused to use (ADR 0010): the ring is corrupt and the driver reads nothing more from it (spec/command-ring.md, Unblocking). | A client wrote an impossible tail: a buggy binding or a hostile process, which the ring cannot name. Every client's commands now time out. Restart the driver, which recreates the ring; if the counter climbs again, stop clients one at a time until it stops, and look for a binding that was upgraded or does not conform to spec/command-ring.md. |
| 11 | `command_ring.rejected_record` | counter | static | Records the driver found outside the command ring's bounds, a length or type no client writes by the protocol (ADR 0010): the driver reads nothing more from the ring (spec/command-ring.md, Reading). | A client wrote a corrupt command: a buggy binding or a hostile process, which the ring cannot name. Every client's commands now time out. Restart the driver, which recreates the ring; if the counter climbs again, stop clients one at a time until it stops, and look for a binding that was upgraded or does not conform to spec/command-ring.md. |
| 12 | `client.timed_out` | counter | static | Clients the driver timed out because no command of theirs arrived within the client liveness timeout; their publications and subscriptions were removed and a client timeout event sent (spec/client-protocol.md, Liveness and timeouts). | A client stopped sending keepalives: it is stuck, paused under a debugger, or its conductor thread died. Its own driver timeout closes it. Find the process by the client id in the client timeout event and look at what stopped its conductor. |
| 13 | `client_protocol.rejected_command` | counter | static | Commands the driver refused at decoding, for their channel or for a field outside its bound: a message too short to carry a correlation id, an unknown type, a message of the wrong length, a bad string, a channel that is not cavalry:ipc, or a replay length below -1 (spec/client-protocol.md, What the driver rejects); the client got an error event when its correlation id was readable. | A client sent a command the protocol does not allow: a binding that does not conform to spec/client-protocol.md or was upgraded apart from the driver. The error event names the command; stop that client and check its version against the driver's. |
| 14 | `client_protocol.errors` | counter | static | Error events the driver sent, whatever the code: every command this version refused after the ring delivered it (spec/client-protocol.md, Error codes); the causes with a counter of their own are client_protocol.rejected_command, driver.registry_full and driver.log_create_failed. | Compare with client_protocol.rejected_command, driver.registry_full and driver.log_create_failed; an error none of them explains is code 2, 3 or 11, a client naming a registration the driver does not know, or a bug the error event's message names. |
| 15 | `driver.registry_full` | counter | static | Commands refused with error code 10 because the driver's registry of clients, publications, subscriptions or images, or the counters file, was at capacity (spec/client-protocol.md, Sizes). | A fixed capacity of the driver is reached: clients, publications or subscriptions are not being closed, or this host needs more than one driver's worth. Close what is not used; the error event's message names the registry; the capacities are the driver's in this version. |
| 16 | `driver.log_create_failed` | counter | static | Log buffers the driver could not create or size, refused with error code 12: the filesystem under the driver directory is full or not writable (spec/client-protocol.md, Commands). | Free space on the filesystem under the driver directory (/dev/shm on Linux): each cavalry:ipc publication needs 3 × 64 MiB + 4 KiB there while it is live or lingers. Close publications that are not used, or move the driver directory to a filesystem with room. |
| 17 | `conductor.idle_strategy` | gauge | static | The idle strategy the conductor runs, what its thread does on a duty cycle that found no work, stored once when the driver starts: 0 backoff, 1 yield, 2 busy-spin. |  |
| 18 | `counters.allocations` | counter | static | Counter allocations made since the driver started, the static counters' own records included: every record that went from unused or reclaimed to allocated, the transition counters.allocated adds one for, so that counters.allocations minus counters.freed is counters.allocated (spec/counters-file.md, Metadata record). |  |
| 19 | `counters.freed` | counter | static | Counters freed since the driver started: every record that went from allocated to reclaimed, the transition counters.allocated loses one for; a reclaimed record is allocated again after the counter reuse timeout. |  |
| 20 | `recording.started` | counter | static | Recordings the driver started: a catalog slot taken, the time index and the first segment file created, the two position counters allocated and recording ready sent (spec/client-protocol.md, Commands). |  |
| 21 | `recording.stopped` | counter | static | Recordings the driver stopped, by stop recording, at a publication's end of stream, or after a failed write or a frame that failed its check; each sent recording stopped with the stop position (spec/client-protocol.md, Commands). |  |
| 22 | `recording.write_failed` | counter | static | Writes or syncs the recorder could not make to a recording's segment file or time index, each of which stopped the recording at the position written (spec/client-protocol.md, Commands). | The log directory's filesystem is full, read-only or failing: `cavalry doctor` names it. Free space, or move the log directory with `--log-dir`, then start the recording again; what was written up to the stop position is whole and replayable. |
| 23 | `recording.start_failed` | counter | static | Start recording commands refused with error code 12 because the recording's time index or first segment file could not be created in the log directory (spec/client-protocol.md, Commands). The recording's catalog slot may already be taken: a start that fails at its files leaves its slot valid, stopped at the start position, so the catalog's slots used are at most recording.started plus these plus the driver.registry_full refusals of a start. | Free space on the log directory's filesystem, or move the directory with `--log-dir`; a recording needs a 128 MiB segment file when it starts. |
| 24 | `recording.catalog_full` | counter | static | Start recording commands refused with error code 10 because the catalog holds every one of its 1048576 slots (spec/durable-log.md, Catalog header). | The log directory has held 1048576 recordings in its life: move or archive it, and start the driver on a new directory, which gets a new catalog. |
| 25 | `recording.recovered` | counter | static | Recordings found live, or with a torn stop, when the driver opened the log directory, whose stop fields recovery rebuilt from their files (spec/durable-log.md, The driver). | The previous driver did not stop cleanly; the recordings are whole up to the rebuilt stop. If this climbs at every start, find what kills the driver before `close`. |
| 26 | `recording.invalidated` | counter | static | Catalog slots recovery set to state 2 because their files cannot repair them: an empty slot before the last, a creation checksum that fails, or a segment file missing between the start and the last (spec/durable-log.md, The driver). | A recording in the log directory is damaged beyond repair and `cavalry doctor` names its slot: check the disk, and restore the directory from a backup if the recording matters; the slot is never reused. |
| 27 | `recording.index_rewritten` | counter | static | Time indexes recovery wrote again with their start entry, gave a first entry, or truncated to whole entries in order or to the entries at or before the rebuilt stop (spec/durable-log.md, The driver). |  |
| 28 | `recording.catalog_truncated` | counter | static | Catalog files recovery truncated to whole slots because a crash left bytes past the last slot: 0 or 1 at each driver start (spec/durable-log.md, The driver). |  |
| 29 | `recording.slot_dropped` | counter | static | Empty last catalog slots recovery dropped because a crash tore a recording's creation: 0 or 1 at each driver start, and the next recording takes the id (spec/durable-log.md, The driver). |  |
| 30 | `recording.files_removed` | counter | static | Files recovery removed: segment files wholly past a rebuilt stop, and the files of a deleted recording that were still present (spec/durable-log.md, The driver). |  |
| 31 | `recording.position` | gauge | instance | The position of one recording up to which the recorder has written its segment files, what the operating system holds, stored with a release store after each block; the publisher's limit respects it (spec/log-buffer.md, The driver); key: recording id (i64), little-endian; label text: the recording id, the session id and the stream id in decimal, space-separated. | A recording.position that does not move while its publication.position does is a recorder behind a slow or failing disk, and the publisher is back-pressured when it reaches the window: check recording.write_failed and the log directory's disk with `cavalry doctor`. |
| 32 | `recording.synced_position` | gauge | instance | The position of one recording up to which a sync has made its segment files and time index durable, stored with a release store after each sync, at most a second behind recording.position; key and label as recording.position. | A synced position far behind recording.position is a disk whose sync is slow; a power cut loses what lies between the two. |
| 33 | `replay.started` | counter | static | Replays the driver started: the replay's publication created at the start position, its counters allocated and replay ready sent (spec/client-protocol.md, Commands; ADR 0030). |  |
| 34 | `replay.stopped` | counter | static | Replays that ended, for any reason: each sent replay stopped with the position reached and the reason; replay.ended, replay.not_connected and replay.failed count the reasons other than a stop replay command (spec/client-protocol.md, Commands). |  |
| 35 | `replay.ended` | counter | static | Replays that reached their end position or their recording's stop position, reason 0 of replay stopped: the subscriber saw everything it asked for. |  |
| 36 | `replay.not_connected` | counter | static | Replays the driver ended, reason 2 of replay stopped, because their publication had no subscriber for the replay connect timeout, from the start or from the moment the last subscriber went (spec/client-protocol.md, Liveness and timeouts). | A replay was started with no subscription on its replay stream id and channel, or the subscriber closed before the replay ended: add the subscription before the start replay command, or keep it until replay stopped arrives; the replay ended at the position it had reached and can be started again from there. |
| 37 | `replay.failed` | counter | static | Replays that ended on a failure, reason 3 of replay stopped: a segment file of the recording could not be read, or a frame in it failed a check, which log_buffer.rejected_frame counts as well; the position in the event is the last frame delivered. | A recording's segment file is unreadable or damaged: `cavalry doctor` names the recording when its slot is invalid, and the log directory's disk is the first thing to check; what was delivered up to the position is whole, and a replay from that position fails at the same frame until the file is restored from a backup. |
| 38 | `replay.start_failed` | counter | static | Start replay commands refused after the driver took them, with error code 21 (a recording id the catalog does not hold as a valid recording), 23 (a position out of range) or 12 (a segment file that could not be opened); a start the registries refuse with code 10 is driver.registry_full's, and a replay log that could not be created is driver.log_create_failed's (spec/client-protocol.md, Commands). | The error event's message names the recording, the position and the recording's bounds, or the file: `cavalry doctor` lists the recordings with their start and stop positions; resolve an instant through the time index before asking for a position, and check the log directory's files for a recording whose segment is missing. |
| 39 | `replay.position` | gauge | instance | The position of one replay up to which the replayer has written the recording's frames into the replay's log, stored with a release store after each block; it moves no faster than the slowest subscriber's position plus the publication window, and not at all with no subscriber (spec/client-protocol.md, Commands); key: replay session id (i64), little-endian; label text: the replay session id, the recording id, the replay publication's session id and its stream id in decimal, space-separated. | A replay.position that does not move while the replay has a subscriber is a subscriber that stopped polling: compare the subscription.position counters of the replay stream; one with no subscriber waits, and ends with reason 2 after the replay connect timeout. |

## State machines

Every state machine on the data plane registers its states and transitions in `counters.toml` too, and `just lint-counters` fails a transition that names no counter, a counter that is not of kind `counter` in the table above, a counter whose constant no code in the enum's crate names, or an enum whose variants are not the machine's states (CLAUDE.md, invariant 4). The enum that holds the states carries the comment `// state machine: <name>` on the line before its definition. The check fails closed: every enum under `crates/*/src` whose name is or ends in `State`, `Status` or `Phase` carries that comment, or `// not a state machine: <why>` with the reason no transition of it needs a counter, and `just lint-counters` names the file and line of one that has neither. Each machine is listed here with the counter every transition adds one to.

### `counters_record`

States: `unused`, `allocated`, `reclaimed`.

| From | To | Counter |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `unused` | `allocated` | `counters.allocations` |
| `reclaimed` | `allocated` | `counters.allocations` |
| `allocated` | `reclaimed` | `counters.freed` |

### `catalog_slot`

States: `empty`, `valid`, `invalid`, `deleted`.

| From | To | Counter |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `empty` | `valid` | `recording.started` |
| `empty` | `valid` | `recording.start_failed` |
| `empty` | `valid` | `driver.registry_full` |
| `empty` | `invalid` | `recording.invalidated` |
| `valid` | `invalid` | `recording.invalidated` |
| `deleted` | `invalid` | `recording.invalidated` |

### `recording`

States: `starting`, `live`, `stopped`, `failed`.

| From | To | Counter |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `starting` | `live` | `recording.started` |
| `starting` | `failed` | `recording.start_failed` |
| `starting` | `failed` | `recording.catalog_full` |
| `starting` | `failed` | `driver.registry_full` |
| `live` | `stopped` | `recording.stopped` |
| `live` | `stopped` | `recording.write_failed` |
| `live` | `stopped` | `log_buffer.rejected_frame` |
| `failed` | `stopped` | `recording.stopped` |

### `replay`

States: `starting`, `live`, `stopped`, `failed`.

| From | To | Counter |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `starting` | `live` | `replay.started` |
| `starting` | `failed` | `replay.start_failed` |
| `starting` | `failed` | `driver.registry_full` |
| `starting` | `failed` | `driver.log_create_failed` |
| `live` | `stopped` | `replay.stopped` |
| `live` | `stopped` | `replay.ended` |
| `live` | `stopped` | `replay.not_connected` |
| `live` | `stopped` | `replay.failed` |
| `live` | `stopped` | `log_buffer.rejected_frame` |
